criteria.text: `capability.audit`/`capability.approve` resolve over the shared `crabgic_gateway` registry against a stub MCP client; `capability.approve` rejects a call lacking a pre-minted `trust approve` token.

citations.quotedAssertion: CLAUSE ONE, the half that had no bearer at all. Both tools resolve over the REAL production registry through a REAL MCP transport — `buildRealGatewayToolRegistry` (the registry the shipped `crabgic gateway mcp` command composes) booted with `connectGatewayMcpStdio` over `PassThrough` streams. The span opens on the anti-vacuity assertion, deliberately: :147 'expect(tools.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);' — an empty tool list would otherwise make every `find` below return undefined and the two assertions would read as absence rather than as nothing being served. Then, inside a loop over both tool names: :151 'expect(tool, `${name} is not served by the real registry`).toBeDefined();' and :152 'expect(tool?.description ?? "").not.toBe("");'. NOTE, a strengthening rather than a wording fix: the criterion asks for a stub MCP client and this is a real MCP SDK client. Strictly stronger; no wording correction is claimed or needed.

The fail-closed behaviour, driven through a real `tools/call` rather than at the plain-function level: :214 'expect(refused, `expected a refusal, got: ${JSON.stringify(response)}`).toBe(true);' / :217 'expect(text).not.toMatch(/\bapproved\b/i);' / :221 'expect(text).toMatch(/no audited capability is stored under digest/i);'. The third assertion NAMES THE LAYER that refused, which is what stops the test silently starting to pass for a different reason. Refusal is asserted as a negative on approval rather than by matching a message string, because a message match can succeed against both the refusal and the success path — the failure shape this repository has already recorded for verdict-string assertions.

THE CONTROL that makes the two above mean something — an unknown tool name is refused: :240 'expect(response?.["error"] !== undefined || result?.isError === true).toBe(true);'. Without it, a transport that answered every `tools/call` affirmatively would let the refusal test pass for the wrong reason, and one that refused everything would leave the `tools/list` test green over nothing wired.

CLAUSE TWO — the token clause — which the new suite deliberately does NOT bear, and says so about itself. Unchanged, and still here: :93 'expect(result.approved).toBe(false);' / :94 'expect(store.load(saved.key)?.report.decision).toBe("pending");' / :96 'expect(journal.entries).toHaveLength(0);' for a fabricated, never-minted token — no approval, no state change, and no journal entry. LINE-NUMBER CORRECTION, made here rather than left to rot: the superseded record, the defect record and the roadmap annotation all wrote this span as 93-95. The third assertion is on :96; :95 is the comment above it. Every copy of the old span was grepped before correcting it — three, of which this record and the roadmap annotation are rewritten here, and the third is sha-pinned defect prose left as its own capture. Relabelled from PARTIAL: with clause one now borne, this is the criterion's SECOND clause, complete.

criteria.notes: THE CLAUSE SPLIT, taken verbatim from the bearer's own doc comment rather than from a summary of it — because the two disagree and the file is the authority on itself. `packages/cli/src/gateway-mcp/capability-tools-over-stdio.test.ts` states that the refusal it observes is produced by the DIGEST guard ('no audited capability is stored under digest'), NOT by the token check: 'Mutating only the token-verification seam leaves this green, because the digest guard returns first. Only removing BOTH guards, so the tool genuinely approves, reddens it (measured: 1 failed / 18 passed).' It therefore bears the criterion's FIRST clause and explicitly 'does NOT bear the second clause about a missing pre-minted `trust approve` token'. That clause stays borne by `packages/detect/src/mcp/capability-approve-handler.test.ts:93-96`, cited above (the span is 93-96, not the 93-95 three earlier records wrote — :95 is a comment). Anyone describing this bearer as closing the token clause is describing the wrong test. STRONGER THAN THE WORDING ASKS, and this is a note rather than a `WORDING-MISMATCH`: the criterion says 'against a stub MCP client'; the suite drives the REAL production registry (`buildRealGatewayToolRegistry`, the one the shipped `crabgic gateway mcp` command composes) over a REAL MCP SDK server (`connectGatewayMcpStdio` on `PassThrough` streams). A criterion satisfied by something strictly stronger needs no wording correction. WHAT THE GAP WAS. The criterion's own named evidence, `packages/detect/src/mcp/tool-definitions.test.ts`, was relocated in `5c21a0f` and DELETED in `c39292c` with the hand-rolled stdio server it drove — a correct deletion (that server could never dispatch `tools/call`) that simply never re-established the assertion against the MCP SDK server replacing it. Registry membership was still proven (`build-tool-registry.test.ts`) and the transport was still proven generically (`stdio-boot.test.ts`), but the two were never composed, which is exactly the hop where a schema or naming mistake in `build-tool-registry.ts`'s re-declaration of these two tools would first surface. THE FLIP IS EVIDENCE-REPRODUCED, not EVIDENCE-EXISTS: the suite was re-run locally at this tree, 1 file / 3 tests passed, captured in the transcript. Coverage was disabled for that scoped run because the repo-wide 80% gate cannot be met by a single file; what is asserted is the test COUNT, not the exit code. PER-PUSH EXECUTION is proven by the job-log delta pair above rather than by a green workflow badge — a green workflow proves the workflow passed, never that this test ran in it. RELATED ITEMS DISCHARGED, per the defect record's own 'Related, not part of this defect' section: `docs/evidence/phase-12/README.md`'s mapping row for this criterion and its carry-forward (b) both carry dated 2026-08-06 in-line corrections, added without moving a single line of that file.
